attendees.role: special education staff, presenter (team chair/school psychologist)

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reported a legislative bill sponsored by MASC, MASS, MTA and AFT that would apply an inflation adjustment to Chapter 70; a MASC representative told her it would bring Lunenburg new funding if passed.

The chair said the town is not a held-harmless community; it got a small percentage increase last year after its low-income count rose, which is more than held-harmless towns get but far less than other communities receive.

budget_items.topic: Circuit breaker reimbursement rate / proposed 100% bill
budget_items.what_was_said: Committee discussed a bill proposing 100% reimbursement of special education circuit-breaker costs; a member clarified the current formula reimburses after districts cover four times foundation, and there is confusion whether the bill means 100% of the current 75% rate or a new 100% rate.
The chair reported the amount of warrants signed for the period, directing questions to the superintendent's office.
A committee member asked how much was spent designing the stormwater BMP without consulting the school district first; the presenter estimated the range for the engineering design work.
The chair said a legislator has been pushing for an earmark tied to enhanced 911 funding for the town that could come through now that the override passed.

budget_items.topic: Box Tops for Education donation, Primary School
budget_items.what_was_said: A check from Box Tops for Education was recommended for acceptance into the primary school's gift account, to support upcoming school trips.

budget_items.topic: Box Tops for Education donation, Turkey Hill
budget_items.what_was_said: A second Box Tops for Education check was recommended for acceptance into the Turkey Hill Elementary gift account.

A speaker explained the override was set at the modest amount needed to level-fund schools versus the prior year minus expiring ESSER funds, not to expand programs; some positions will still be cut as planned.
The chair noted the state's millionaire's tax has collected more revenue than expected, which legislators are looking to direct toward education and transportation.
A speaker thanked everyone who participated in the town vote on the override.

decisions.decision: Superintendent will have the business/facilities staff prepare an informational slide deck on student activity fees for a June meeting.
Committee members agreed to send the chair proposed topics for the legislative delegation before the next meeting so a combined session can be scheduled.
A building/facility maintenance plan will be added to the committee's list of goals but is not expected soon given the facilities director's current workload.
Completed superintendent evaluations are due to be submitted by June 5th ahead of the June 12th meeting.
Committee agreed to place ARPA funds, which some feel should be returned, on a future agenda for discussion.

minutes.summary: This School Committee meeting was largely a post-override celebration and reporting session: public comment and the chair's report thanked voters, staff, and advocates for the town's successful override vote, which will level-fund schools (offsetting expiring ESSER money) without expanding programs. The committee voted to reject a proposed rainwater retention/stormwater demonstration project at the middle-high school after learning it was sited without consulting the district and had already cost several thousand dollars in engineering, and voted not to increase school choice seats to protect small class sizes; it also received presentations on a new family-school partnership compact, the state's new IEP form, and facilities project updates.

what_happened.line: The town's override passed, which will level-fund the schools by offsetting expiring ESSER money rather than add programs.
The committee voted to reject a rainwater retention project proposed for the middle-high school after learning it was sited without district input and had already run up engineering costs.
The committee voted not to increase school choice seats for next year, to protect current class sizes.
Members agreed to gather topics for a joint session with the legislative delegation, covering bills on Chapter 70 and special-education circuit-breaker reimbursement.

why_it_matters: The override outcome sets what the schools can spend this year; residents already voted on it, and this meeting explains why the budget holds steady rather than expands.
Rejecting the stormwater project affects how a town-proposed site project at the middle-high school gets planned and who signs off on it before design money is spent.
Holding school choice seats flat affects class sizes and the revenue those seats would otherwise bring the district.
